title: UPDATE: Reef Shark and Shore with Opus 5 - algae and multiplayer added.
author: octaviustf
selftext:
Probably spent more time on this than I needed to but I was having fun and got some nice feedback from community.  This video shows the algae displacing as sharks and other creatures swim through it - it's very satisfying!  
  
I also added multiplayer so if anyone wants to join my reef and swim around or create their own reef and invite friends the app is live here: [https://shoreplay.app/](https://shoreplay.app/) \- you can generate a shark from 8 species and then watch your shark swim or take control if you want to guide it around.  

Sometimes gamedev is super lonely so if you're bored take a swim with me or some friends :).

comments.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
comments.body: What tools/prompt did you use? Those graphics are very impressive. It looks beyond what Claude usually does in three.js.

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Thanks - I used Claude Artifacts to create the voxel sharks and animations- then imported code into a Claude Code project.  I started with sea floor, caustics, lighting, then the water surface shader - then added in the sharks, movement. I used Artifacts for the procedural fish and the corral props as well.

replies.author: WHITESTAFRlCAN
replies.body: Could you go into more detail of how you built it, I am assuming you use claude code since you said max subscriber, did you use a game engine? what did you do for assets / art?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: No I did not use any engine- 3js - also no outside assets or art- all procedurally generated with Claude - I used Claude Artifacts with a prompt like "make detailed voxel tiger shark in 3js with animations". Then built from there.

replies.author: Electronic-Koala2088
replies.body: So within the claude framework, how large can it create the world? and if you wante d an MMO style with this art, how far can it get?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: I had an infinitely long procedural shoreline initially- issue with that and MMO is that sharks rarely see each other.  Currently the game (app) is multiplayer - I'm not sure limits of number of players in terms of bandwidth etc but could scale up fairly easily I think at least on desktop.  The art is very performant

comments.author: rapkannibale
comments.body: What’s your tech stack if you don’t mind sharing? Looks really good!

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: thanks! It's 100% Claude (Max setting) - I utilized Artifacts for the "detail work" like the animated voxel sharks, the procedural cora, the fish.  Then I used Claude Code to integrate everything- create the seafloor, lighting, algae, etc.  There weren't any other integrations in terms of art, etc.  Just 3js.   I have found voxels to be the best approach for me anyways for getting decent looking procedural models.

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: Very cool. Did you provide a reference image of the shark and ask to recreate it using voxels and three.js or did Claude come up with the shark design by itself?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: 100% no reference images- I was really impressed at the accuracy- it even made different species have slightly different animations and speed settings.

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: Wow nice. Sorry for all the questions. I’m trying to learn to use Claude more effectively. Did you use Claude code on desktop or the CLI?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: I use Desktop - what I do is use Claude Artifacts via Claude browser as well as Claude Code in Desktop app.  I have found Max setting to be better than High for example.  I rarely use Ultracode. No worries about the questions!

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: Thanks. What exactly are artifacts in Claude browser? You just ask it to generate a voxel shark artifact using 3js for example?

replies.author: octaviustf
replies.body: Artifacts is really good for like small scope detailed single file apps/demos/prototypes or in my case creating procedural voxel models. Yes you ask it to generate a voxel shark for example in 3JS- then you can tune and iterate visually
